To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a wearable 8-channel EEG acquisition system has been developed, which can be integrated with other sensors in a Body Area Network (BAN) and can measure EEG and ETI simultaneously.

the proposed 8-channel gel-less active-electrode EEG/ ETI acquisition system has a high common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) of 84 dB, low input referred noise (IRN) of 1.75 uVrms, high electrode offset rejection (EOR) of 0.25V and high input impedance of 1.2GΩ.
the proposed system has: 1) low power consumption, 2) high input impedance, 3) low input noise, 4) high CMRR, 5) low output impedance and 6) high ETI measurement range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a wearable EEG acquisition system, which can be integrated into body area networks (BANs) for long-term, continuous EEG recordings.
the design of a novel 8-channel active-electrode EEG/ ETI acquisition system.
the design and implementation of a low-cost, low-power, wearable, gel-free 8-channel EEG/ETI acquisition system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is capable of recording EEG signals from the human body, and is able to measure electrode impedance, while maintaining high input impedance and low noise.
the system presented here is a promising candidate for future wearable EEG/ETI acquisition systems.
the system has been successfully developed and is capable of recording high quality EEG and ETI measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel 8-channel active-electrode EEG/impedance acquisition system, consisting a novel 8-Channel active-electrode (AE) EEG amplifier and a single back-end (BE), capable of recording EEG/impedence signals.
we have developed the first wearable, low power and high performance EEG/ETI acquisition system for body area networks.
we have successfully developed a wearable, active electrode based EEG/ETI acquisition system, which can be used in BANs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed active-electrode EEG/ ETI acquisition system is suitable for wearable applications, such as body area networks (BANs).
the AEs can be configured to measure EEG and ETI, while the CMFF scheme boosts the CMR of the AE pairs.
it is possible to implement a high performance active electrode EEG acquisition system in a standard CMOS process.
